issues.legal_issue: An appeal cannot be dismissed solely because the appellant transferred the disputed interest during its pendency and the transferee did not seek to continue the proceedings.
material_facts: The appellant had brought a suit seeking a declaration of title and restoration of possession, and appealed after the suit was dismissed.
While the appeal was pending, the appellant released her interest in the property to her daughter, who later transferred the property to another person.
The High Court dismissed the appeal because the appellant had transferred her interest and therefore could not continue it.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in dismissing the appeal on that ground. Its judgment was set aside, and the appeal was remitted for a fresh decision after hearing the parties.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXII Rules 10 and 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a transfer or devolution of interest during a suit or appeal does not automatically terminate the proceeding. The original party may continue it even after ceasing to have an interest, while a transferee may seek leave to continue the proceeding but is not required to do so; failure to seek leave does not require dismissal. The transferee is ordinarily bound by the result and may benefit from it, subject to a properly constituted challenge based on matters such as improper prosecution or collusion. The Court relied on Dhurandhar Prasad Singh v. Jai Prakash University and Jaskirat Datwani v. Vidyavati.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is an appeal brought after a lower court dismissed a suit.
predicates.interest_transferred_during_appeal: A party to the appeal transfers or releases an interest in the disputed subject matter while the appeal is pending.
predicates.appeal_dismissed_solely_for_transfer: The appeal is dismissed solely because the appellant transferred that interest during the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a party transfers an interest during an appeal and the appeal is dismissed solely for that reason, the appeal is not dismissed on account of the transfer.
